subject: Post-call: SummitOps inference capacity & SLOs — recap and action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@summitops.com>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@summitops.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-23T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — SummitOps latency/throughput needs and next steps

Hi Tom / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed mutual action plan so we’re aligned. Summary points below; I focused on decisions we can make quickly to scope a short POC.

Key pain & goals
- Current pain: user-facing search & alerting is inconsistent under peak, p95 response spikes to ~950ms and some requests time out during batch processing windows.
- Business goal: reduce p95 inference latency to <= 150ms under typical user load, support sustained 600 rps for search traffic during peak windows, and keep cold-start recovery <= 3s.

Technical constraints you shared
- Model: currently evaluating an LLM reranker + short-generation pipeline; baseline is a fine-tuned 13B model.
- Data residency: all inference must run in our us-east cloud and log-level retention limited to 30 days.
- Security: SOC2 evidence requested as part of procurement (you’ll send questionnaire).

Initial Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Deployment topology: Dedicated pool in us-east (reserved) with autoscaling headroom for 800rps burst; primary model: 13B quantized (int8) variant for quality parity, fallback: 7B quantized for sub-100ms p95 for simple reranks.
- Runtime levers: use prefix KV caching for session affinity on repeated queries, adaptive batching with 30ms latency cap, and per-route routing so search uses dedicated low-latency nodes.
- SLO targets to validate in POC: p50 45–60ms, p95 <= 150ms, cold-start <= 3s, throughput sustained 600rps with 10% CPU/GPU headroom.

Mutual action plan (proposed timeline)
- This week (by Fri 09/24): SummitOps to share the SOC2 questionnaire and a small sample of production request traces (anonymized) — Maya to send.
- Next week (target 09/30): Redwood will provide a topology sketch + estimated Dedicated pool size and cost for a 30-day POC (attached: rough topology sketch and cost model).
- POC kickoff week (aim week of 10/07): 2-week POC: integration with your test cluster, run synthetic load + replay traces, and measure p95/p50 and cold-start.

Open questions we flagged
- Do you have heavy long-sequence (>1024 tokens) requests that must go to the 13B model (Tom)?
- What percentage of requests are rerank-only vs generation (Maya asked for a breakdown).

Attachments: I attached the topology sketch and a POC cost spreadsheet.

Next steps: Maya, can you share the traces and questionnaire? Connor / Neha — I’ll need a quick sizing review so we can lock costs by EOW.

Thanks again —

— Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Greene <tom.greene@summitops.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@summitops.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-23T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SummitOps latency/throughput needs and next steps

Thanks Soojin — solid recap. Couple clarifications:

- About sequence length: ~95% of requests are short (<=256 tokens). The remaining 5% are long-form summaries that we can route to a slower path during the POC.
- Rerank vs gen: roughly 70% rerank-only (candidate scoring), 30% short generation (confirmation text, <100 tokens).

I’ll have Maya drop the anonymized traces and SOC2 questionnaire by EOD tomorrow. For the POC, we prefer a hosted dedicated lane but are open to a VPC private deploy if the compliance team asks.

Also: any concerns about int8 quant for your 13B variant on quality? We care about not regressing on top-K precision for rerank.

— Tom
Sr. Eng Manager, SummitOps
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Greene <tom.greene@summitops.com>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@summitops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-24T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SummitOps latency/throughput needs and next steps

Tom — quick technical note on quantization and quality:

- We generally recommend an evaluation matrix: run accuracy/regression checks on the quantized int8 13B variant vs your current float baseline on a representative testset (we can help run this in the POC). In practice we see negligible top-K precision drop for reranking when we use per-channel symmetric quantization + 16-bit KV accumulation.
- Fallback strategy: route low-latency traffic to 7B-int8 for quick reranks (p95 < 120ms) and use 13B-int8 for re-ranking full-context requests. We can also enable a hybrid KV caching policy so commonly requested prefixes never hit full model compute.
- For throughput planning: to sustain 600rps at p95 <= 150ms we estimate a Dedicated pool of 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs with our batching profile and prefix cache assumptions; exact VM/GPU mix TBD after we see traces.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SummitOps latency/throughput needs and next steps

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround, Tom. Maya / Tom: once we have the traces I’ll schedule a 30-minute sizing call with Connor and Rishi to validate the 8xA100 estimate and confirm the topology (dedicated vs private VPC).

Action checklist (updated)
- SummitOps: send anonymized traces + SOC2 questionnaire (Maya) — target 2027-09-24 EOD.
- Redwood: produce POC topology sketch + cost estimate (Soojin / Connor) — target 2027-09-30.
- Redwood: prepare regression test harness for quantized 13B vs float baseline (Neha) — ready for POC start.

I’ve attached the topology sketch and a preliminary POC spreadsheet (cost + telemetry checkpoints). If anything needs to change on timing, please flag.

Best,
— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
